meeting_header: Date: 2026-04-05 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 54m | Location: Zoom | Recorded | Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Crestfall Head of MLOps), Marcus Reed (CTO), Leah Turner (Platform Eng), Samir Qureshi (Security)
summary: Kickoff for Sprint 0 onboarding. Reviewed deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC), security posture and immediate integration tasks for network and identity. Agreed next steps: share security pack, supply VPC details, run short dedicated perf check and confirm logging/retention needs.
topics: Deployment mode decision: Dedicated pool vs Private VPC
Initial perf benchmarks: batching, KV cache, sequence lengths
Rollout plan: canary, model pinning, fallback policies
transcript: [00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Sofia Ramirez, AE on the Redwood side. Liam our SE is with me. we have about 50 minutes, want to run intake for Sprint 0 - network, security, quick performance sanity checks, and next steps.

[00:28] Aisha: Thanks Sofia. I'm Aisha, head of MLOps at Crestfall. Marcus is our CTO, Leah does platform, and Samir covers security. timeline is aggressive, we'd like a pilot in the next 3 weeks if possible.
[00:46] Marcus: Just to add, timeline driven by exec ask - pilot must show <200ms p95 for our chat use case, and costs need to be within x1.5 of our current baseline. we'll balance latency vs cost.
[01:12] Liam: Got it. quick clarifying q, is that 200ms p95 for user-visible generation or end-to-end including your app? sometimes network adds 50-80ms.
[01:26] Marcus: Good point. that's end-to-end with our API gateway, so we should budget network. Our internal goal is ~120ms server-side p95.
[01:44] Leah: For infra context, we're on AWS in us-west-2, we run Kubernetes EKS for other services. we'll likely prefer a VPC peering model but open to dedicated if the isolation is better.

[02:05] Sofia: Perfect. so three main paths: Redwood Hosted (fastest onboarding), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + isolation), or Redwood Private (customer VPC & private control plane). each has tradeoffs on latency, cost and operational overhead.
[02:30] Samir: Security first: we need SOC2 evidence, audit log retention options, KMS integration guidance — can Redwood support CMK/HSM for key management?

[02:48] Sofia: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS keys for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can offer integration patterns and for Hosted we have envelope encryption and SOC2 docs. i'll share the security pack after this call.
[03:06] Samir: Cool. also, do you support SAML/SSO and RBAC for console access? we can't have open accounts for engineers.
[03:18] Liam: We do SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and role-based access in the console. we'll include a runbook for least-privilege roles and token rotation.

[03:33] Aisha: On traffic profile: most requests are short chat turns, mean tokens ~80, tail sometimes 512 for long context. we also have embedding use few times per minute. curious if prefix cache or KV-cache is easy to enable.

[03:51] Liam: Redwood runtime supports KV cache/prefix caching and automatic detection for repeated prefixes. for your token distribution, caching + batching will be helpful to reduce cost without blowing latency.
[04:08] Marcus: How mature is the quantization and kernel selection? we have mixed workloads; some models are 7b, a couple 13b research variants.

[04:20] Liam: We pick kernels at runtime based on model architecture and sequence length distribution, and we can recommend quantization profiles per-model. for 7b you'll see best ops with int8 profiles; we'll run a quick bench.
[04:38] Leah: Network question: for VPC peering, do you need a NAT or can you do cross-account peering? we have strict egress controls.

[04:50] Sofia: For Private VPC we support peering and private link patterns. we'll send sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippets. if egress is blocked, we can work with a transit gateway setup; details in doc.
[05:10] Aisha: On logging, what's the retention granularity and can we forward to our SIEM?
[05:18] Liam: Audit logs can be forwarded to your S3/kinesis or syslog; retention is configurable. for Hosted we keep short retention by default but can enable long-tail retention as an add-on.
[05:35] Marcus: Cost controls — do you expose per-route throttles and token-level billing to our engineers? we want to avoid runaway spend in testing.
[05:48] Sofia: Yes, the Console has per-route quotas, rate limits and token-level cost breakdowns. we'll also provide Optimize recommendations for batching and model selection to meet cost targets.
[06:05] Leah: Great. can we walk the Sprint 0 checklist? what are the minimum deliverables from both sides?

[06:15] Sofia: Sure — from Redwood: security pack (SOC2, encryption/KMS details), VPC peering templates, perf harness & suggested batch settings, and a proposed canary run plan. From Crestfall: network diagram, CIDR ranges, SSO metadata, and representative prompt sets for evals.
[06:38] Aisha: We'll provide prompt sets and some production telemetry samples. the prompts contain PHI-like strings — any concerns about data residency?
[06:50] Samir: yes, we need clarity on in-flight encryption and data-at-rest for Hosted option.
[06:58] Sofia: For Hosted we encrypt at rest and in flight; we recommend Private or Dedicated for stricter residency. will add exact data flow diagrams to the security pack.
[07:12] Marcus: Regarding pilot, can Redwood run a 48h canary under our traffic shape in Dedicated? we'd like to validate p95 and cost delta.

[07:24] Liam: Absolutely. we'll spin a small Dedicated pool that matches your expected concurrency, seed it with model weights you want, run synthetic and sampled live requests. i'll handle the harness.
[07:40] Leah: For the harness, can you share what metrics you'll collect? we want to compare with our APM.
[07:47] Liam: We'll collect token-level latency, p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, KV hit rate, and per-route cost. we'll provide a CSV and a dashboard link.
[08:02] Aisha: Are there known gotchas for EKS + VPC peering? we've had trouble with MTU sizes before.
[08:10] Sofia: MTU and NAT timeouts are common; we'll include recommended MTU settings and keepalive heuristics in the network snippet.
[08:25] Marcus: Security handshake — Samir what do you need from Redwood to sign off?
[08:31] Samir: SOC2 attestation, KMS integration doc, SIEM forwarding examples, and data retention options. also I want a list of supported HSM vendors if Private deploy uses them.
[08:44] Sofia: Noted. action item for me to send that by Wed.
[09:00] Leah: On identity, SCIM provisioning is good. we have a requirement for 'separation of duties' groups for developers vs infra engineers.
[09:12] Liam: Console RBAC supports groups and scoped roles; we'll include a sample mapping: devs = no billing, infra = deploy, ops = full runbook access.
[09:27] Aisha: On model pinning and rollouts, can we pin a model version for the pilot and do canary rollouts for later changes? we need deterministic behavior for tests.
[09:38] Liam: Yes, model pinning and canary policies are first-class. you can route x% to new variant and set automatic fallback if latency or quality regresses.
[09:50] Marcus: About quality regressions, can Redwood tie regression alerts to our eval sets?
[09:56] Sofia: Redwood Optimize supports evals tied to prompts and will raise regression alerts; we'll walk you through setting that up in Sprint 0.
[10:10] Aisha: Great. one more on embeddings — we want to ensure vectors remain private. any default retention on embeddings?
[10:18] Liam: By default embeddings are ephemeral unless you explicitly store them. for Hosted we don't retain embeddings past processing unless you enable storage. we'll document the flow.
[10:32] Leah: Regarding dataset size for the perf bench, we have around 15k daily chat requests and 200 concurrent users during peak. will that be enough to stress GPU pools?
[10:45] Liam: For a canary you'll want to replicate peak concurrency; 200 concurrent users is a good target. we'll recommend a Dedicated pool size accordingly after initial bench runs.

[11:00] Sofia: ok let's capture immediate risks: 1) network timeline for peering, 2) KMS/HSM approvals may add delay, 3) prompt sets containing sensitive data need to be redacted for hosted flows. anyone add more?
[11:18] Samir: Need to add regulatory review for certain PHI components. may require a Private deployment if we can't get DPA terms cleared fast enough.
[11:30] Marcus: under that constraint, we should prepare both Dedicated and Private option cost estimates so we can decide after security review.
[11:41] Sofia: Will do. we will prepare side-by-side cost and latency projections for the pilot.
[11:48] Leah: Ops handover - who will be our point of contact for infra issues during pilot?
[11:55] Sofia: Liam will be primary SE contact; i'll coordinate solution-level escalation. Liam: confirm?
[12:02] Liam: Confirmed. i'll be the primary for performance and infra during pilot and will set up a slack channel with your team.
[12:12] Aisha: Slack channel is helpful. also can Redwood provide a short 'how we measure p95' doc so we're consistent?
[12:20] Sofia: yes, we have a measurement page; will include P95 definition, sampling cadence and owned dashboards.
[12:30] Marcus: any blockers from your side on credentials sharing and Vault access? we usually use HashiCorp Vault for secrets.
[12:40] Liam: We can integrate with Vault via IAM roles and short-lived tokens for Private; we'll share the recommended pattern.
[12:51] Aisha: ok, sounds good. let's talk timeline. if security pack delivered Wed and our network diagram by Fri, could we start the bench next Tue?
[13:02] Sofia: that's realistic. so target: security docs 2026-04-07, network diagram 2026-04-09, bench kickoff 2026-04-13. we'll tentatively schedule the canary window 2026-04-15 to 04-17.
[13:20] Leah: we'll try to get CIDR ranges and a jumpbox window for peering during April 10-12 evenings to reduce service impact.
[13:30] Samir: one procedural q - how do we handle incident postmortems for pilot if something goes wrong? who owns it?

[13:38] Sofia: We'll follow standard SRE ops: immediate triage jointly, Redwood SE will lead product/runtime analysis and Crestfall leads application-level troubleshooting. agreed to share postmortem template.
[13:55] Marcus: any questions about billing or contracts before we wrap?
[14:03] Sofia: commercial point - we'll send a pilot quote for Dedicated for the 48h run and include optional private deployment estimates. legal can send DPAs concurrently.
[14:16] Aisha: Please include cost-per-1000-tokens estimate for the different profiles so we can model it.
[14:25] Sofia: yes, will include token-level estimates and suggested batching settings to meet your cost target.
[14:35] Liam: i'll attach the initial perf harness and a quick script to replay sampled traffic; it will produce the GPU util and latency CSVs.
[14:45] Leah: we'll prepare environment and provide access to a staging prefix for the replay tests.
[14:58] Sofia: ok wrapping up. recap of next steps: security pack, network diagram, perf harness + bench, tentative canary dates. action items listed in follow-up email.
[15:12] Marcus: thanks everyone, this was productive. Looking forward to the security docs and the bench.
[15:20] Aisha: thanks Sofia, Liam, and team. we'll aim for the deadlines.
[15:27] Sofia: Thanks all. we'll share notes and the links. end call.
[15:30] (recording ends)
